definitions.explanation: Describes someone or something that is not good-looking. Can be quite rude when said about a person.
Describes something done without skill or finesse. From the original meaning of {不細工|ぶさいく} (lacking fine craftsmanship).

examples.japanese: ⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ことブサイクだ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{思|おも}う→思う：00492_omou⟧。
ブサイク⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{性格|せいかく}→性格：03371_seikaku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦よければ→いい：00118_ii⟧モテる。
examples.english: Even if you're not attractive, you can be popular if you have a good personality.

examples.japanese: ブサイクな⟦{顔|かお}→顔：00558_kao⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{写真|しゃしん}→写真：00753_shashin⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{写|うつ}って→写る：11494_utsuru⟧しまった。
examples.english: I ended up making an ugly face in the photo.

examples.japanese: ブサイクな⟦{仕上|しあ}がり→仕上がり：07432_shiagari⟧になった。
⟦{字|じ}→字：01606_ji⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ブサイク⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{恥|は}ずかしい→恥ずかしい：00843_hazukashii⟧。
examples.english: My handwriting is clumsy and I'm embarrassed.

examples.japanese: ⟦ラッピング→ラッピング：08317_rappingu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ブサイクだった⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦やり{直|なお}した→やり直す：03172_yarinaosu⟧。
examples.english: The wrapping looked sloppy, so I redid it.

notes:
WRITING:
Written in kanji as {不細工|ぶさいく}, literally "lacking fine craftsmanship." The katakana spelling ブサイク is more common in casual writing.

WATCH OUT:
Calling someone ブサイク directly is very rude. It's mainly used self-deprecatingly, in comedy, or among very close friends. Using it about others behind their back is considered mean.

RELATED SLANG:
- ブス: ugly (even ruder, mainly about women — use with extreme caution)
- ⟦イケメン→イケメン：04761_ikemen⟧: good-looking man (positive counterpart)
